public_rationale: Marcus said object-permanence-type problems held true of all models, including the Sora released the week of his December 11, 2024 post. On December 9, 2024, TechCrunch reported Marques Brownlee's hands-on review of the new Sora. Brownlee said it had the same flaws as other generative tools, namely object-permanence issues, with objects disappearing and reappearing without reason (e1). The same day, OpenAI's launch post said the deployed Sora 'often generates unrealistic physics' (e2). The VideoPhy benchmark (version dated October 3, 2024) tested open and closed video models, including CogVideoX, Lumiere and Dream Machine. Its best model, CogVideoX-5B, made videos that followed both the caption and physical laws in 39.6% of cases (e3). The claim holds on a plain reading that covers the leading evaluated models, not literally every model.
limitations: 'All models' cannot be checked literally. The evidence covers only the models reviewed or benchmarked.
VideoPhy measures caption adherence and physical commonsense broadly, not object permanence specifically. It did not test Sora.
The Sora finding comes from one reviewer's hands-on testing, as reported by TechCrunch.
OpenAI's statement refers to unrealistic physics in general and does not name object permanence.
